'''Takei Ōtomonushi no Kami''' (武居大伴主神, historical kana: たけゐおほともぬしのかみ) is a {{ill|Kami|en|Kami|qid=Q524158|lt=Kami}} associated with local folklore and the {{ill|Suwa Shrine|ja|諏訪信仰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Faith|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 諏訪神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2370082}} in the {{ill|Suwa Region|ja|諏訪地方|lt=Suwa region}} of {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}.

== Overview ==

The deity's name is also written as '''Takei Ōtomo no Kami''', '''Takei Ebisu''', or '''Takei Emishi'''. Additionally, the 'Suwa Shimosha Daihōri Takei Kei Diagram' identifies "Takei Ebisu no Kami" as a distinct deity, considered the child of Takei Ōtomo no Kami.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1185913/45 |title=Suwa Shimosha Daihōri Takei Kei Diagram |publisher=Suwa Historical Collection |date=1938}}</ref>

Takei Ōtomonushi is regarded as one of the original deities of the Suwa region. According to legend, {{ill|Takeminakata|en|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata}} (Suwa Myōjin), enshrined at {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}}, encountered resistance from Takei Ōtomonushi and {{ill|Moreya|en|Moreya|qid=Q11146526|lt=Moreya no Kami}}. However, both were defeated and subsequently became vassals of Takeminakata.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/765072/29 |title=Guardian Gods and Takei Ōtomonushi |publisher=Shinano History Collection |date=1910}}</ref> Other versions suggest disputes between Moreya and Takeminakata over entering Suwa.<ref>Yamada Hajime, 'Takei Ōtomonushi as a Vassal,' Suwa Daimyōjin, 1929.</ref>

According to the traditions of {{ill|Tateshina Shrine|ja|蓼科神社}} in {{ill|Tateshina, Nagano|en|Tateshina, Nagano|qid=Q1346895|lt=Tateshina}}, Takei Ōtomonushi surrendered his territory to Takeminakata and ascended Mount Tateshina.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tateshina Shrine|url=http://www.nagano-jinjacho.jp/shibu/03tousin/02kitasaku/2121.htm|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref>

== Genealogy ==

Takei Ōtomonushi is considered the ancestor of the {{ill|Takei Horibe (Suwa Taisha)|ja|武居祝}} priestly lineage, which was historically managed by the {{ill|Imai Clan (Suwa)|ja|今井氏}}.<ref>Ōta Ryō, ‘Shinano,’ Isobe Kōyōdō, 1924.</ref>

== Shrines ==

[[File:蛭子社（武居会美酒） - Takei-Ebisu Shrine.jpg|thumb|<center>Ebisu Shrine (Takei Ebisu)</center>]]

* {{ill|Takei Ebisu Shrine|ja|武居恵比須社}} (Shimosuwa, Suwa District, Nagano Prefecture)

**Located behind the {{ill|Autumn Shrine|ja|秋宮}} of Suwa Taisha Shimosha. Dedicated to {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|en|Ebisu (mythology)|qid=Q1129330|lt=Ebisu}}.

* {{ill|Hiruko Shrine|ja|蛭子社}} (Takei Ebisu) (Suwa City)

**One of the subordinate shrines of Suwa Taisha Kamisha. Includes the ruins of Takei Hata and Takei Castle.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Takei Hata Ruins|url=https://suwacitymuseum.jp/nandemo/koumoku/0100/010212.htm}}</ref>

* {{ill|Ōtomo Shrine (Saku)|ja|大伴神社 (佐久市望月)}} (Saku City, Mochizuki)

**Traditionally linked to Takei Ōtomonushi, though evidence is speculative.<ref>‘Saku County Gazetteer,’ 1983.</ref>
